top.title: Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds Binance says it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers. Reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to. “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss said. What is frozen Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report . That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it says was affected. Most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts. The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice says government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva said the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action. How the hack unfolded Binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the company said. From there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance. The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has said the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster. That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. The stolen BTC is not covered by those freezes and can be stopped only if it reaches an exchange or service that blocks it. nigeria.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of what he described as the world’s first University of Public Relations and Leadership, as part of efforts to develop a new generation of communication professionals through specialised education, research and professional training. Tinubu announced the approval in a speech delivered by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. The President said a major outcome of Nigeria’s hosting of the global forum was the determination to establish a lasting institutional legacy for the public relations profession. He said: “In this regard, I am pleased to formally approve and support the establishment of the University of Public Relations and Leadership, a first-of-its-kind initiative designed to advance specialised education, research, professional development and leadership training in public relations, strategic communications and related disciplines.” He described the proposed institution as a major investment in human capital and the future of communication, adding that it would provide opportunities to develop communication leaders capable of responding to the demands of a rapidly changing global environment. He urged stakeholders to work together to ensure that the institution developed into a centre of excellence. The President also expressed Nigeria’s appreciation to the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the international public relations community for entrusting the country with the hosting of the global gathering. He described the decision as recognition of Nigeria’s growing contribution to the global communication profession and its capacity to promote responsible communication. Tinubu said hosting the forum provided an opportunity to showcase Nigeria’s people, cultural diversity, economic potential and commitment to constructive international engagement. nigeria.title: Chimamanda’s son’s death: Coroner resumes inquest
nigeria.description: The coroner’s inquest into the death of Nkanu Adichie-Esege, son of Nigerian author Chimamanda Adichie and her husband, Ivara Esege, resumed on Wednesday at the Igbosere Magistrate’s Court in Lagos following a Lagos High Court ruling affirming the coroner’s jurisdiction. The coroner, Magistrate Atinuke Adetunji, resumed proceedings after the High Court dismissed an application by Euracare Hospital seeking to stop the inquest. At Wednesday’s sitting, Taiwo Osipitan, counsel to Euracare Hospital, said it was the first time all parties were appearing before the coroner following the conclusion of proceedings at the High Court. Osipitan said the High Court had ruled that the matter had not reached the stage at which judicial review was necessary and directed that the case be returned to the coroner’s court for continuation of the inquest. He subsequently tendered a copy of the High Court judgment before Adetunji. However, Chukwudi Enebeli, counsel to the deceased’s family, told the court that Euracare’s application was struck out because the coroner’s court had jurisdiction to proceed with the inquest. Enebeli sought an adjournment, explaining that Euracare had only served the parties in open court with the witness statement on oath of Tosin Majekodunmi, a medical doctor. He said the family needed time to examine the statement and determine whether a response would be necessary. Abiodun Loyonu, counsel to Atlantis Paediatric Hospital, also asked the court for an opportunity to respond to Euracare’s witness statement. In her response, the magistrate reminded the parties that the inquest was inquisitorial in nature, adding that guidelines for conducting the proceedings had been discussed at a preliminary meeting held at the commencement of the inquiry. She urged all parties to bear the distinctive nature of the proceedings in mind as the inquest progressed. The coroner also asked whether the parties had filed witness statements on oath in preparation for the hearing. Osipitan, however, sought clarification on whether Lagos State Government officials would be required to file witness statements on oath or could appear in court to give oral evidence if subpoenaed. Adetunji said filing witness statements on oath was not mandatory for such witnesses, adding that government officials summoned through subpoenas could appear before the court and give oral evidence. The parties subsequently agreed that the deceased’s family would lead evidence, followed by Atlantis Paediatric Hospital and Euracare Hospital. The coroner adjourned the inquest to January 19, 20 and 28, 2027. Nkanu, one of Adichie’s twins, died on January 7, 2026, following complications during a series of preparatory medical procedures at Euracare Hospital after being referred from Atlantis Paediatric Hospital. nigeria.title: ADC campaign accuses INEC of bias, demands postponement of mock election test
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, of giving political parties inadequate notice for its November 28 mock accreditation and results collation exercise, demanding its postponement. The Council said the short notice would make it difficult for parties to mobilise, train and deploy agents for the nationwide exercise, warning that the process could undermine confidence in a test designed to assess electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC also faulted INEC’s reported decision not to upload results from Ward, Local Government and State collation levels to its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, during the 2027 elections. The Council said INEC’s November 16 notification, coming barely two days before the November 18 deadline for submitting agents’ names, was unfair, particularly as the exercise would cover all 774 Local Government Areas and two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas. “How does INEC expect political parties to adequately prepare, mobilise, train and submit their agents for an exercise of this magnitude within such a short time? This is not preparation; it is an ambush,” the Council queried. “INEC cannot test electoral credibility through an incredible process.” It demanded an immediate postponement to give political parties sufficient time to nominate agents and participate meaningfully. On electronic transmission of results, the ADC-PCC rejected comments reportedly made by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, that the Commission had neither developed nor tested the system for uploading results from the various collation levels. “Nigerians fought for and demanded real-time electronic transmission of election results precisely to eliminate the manipulation that often occurs between the Polling Unit and subsequent collation levels. “Any attempt to weaken, delay or abandon electronic transmission and public visibility of results at the various levels of collation is an invitation to electoral manipulation,” the Council warned. It recalled that former INEC Chairman, Professor Mahmood Yakubu, had promised to extend result uploads to Ward, Local Government and State levels, adding that his successor, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, had also pledged to strengthen electoral transparency. Questioning the Commission’s apparent change of position, the ADC-PCC asked: “What has changed? Why the sudden retreat from commitments previously made to Nigerians?” It further questioned why Forms EC8B (Ward), EC8C (Local Government) and EC8D (State) could not be uploaded to IReV when the Commission already had the technology to upload polling-unit results on Form EC8A. nigeria.title: Tinubu transmits bill to Reps to decriminalise attempted suicide
nigeria.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026, to the House of Representatives for consideration, seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and provide support for persons who attempt to take their lives. The President’s request was contained in a letter dated November 10, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and read on the floor of the House during plenary on Wednesday. In the letter, Tinubu said the proposed legislation seeks to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021, to remove the criminalisation of attempted suicide and introduce support for affected persons. The President said the transmission was made pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended. The letter, titled, “Transmission of the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for Consideration,” reads in part: “I forward, herewith, the National Mental Health (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for the kind consideration of the House of Representatives.” Explaining the objective of the proposed amendment, Tinubu stated that the bill “seeks to amend the National Mental Health Act, No. 46, 2021 (the ‘Principal Act’) to decriminalise attempted suicide and to provide support to any person who attempts to commit suicide in Nigeria.” He expressed appreciation to the House of Representatives and urged lawmakers to give the proposed legislation expeditious consideration. The proposed amendment, if passed by the National Assembly and assented to by the President, would change the existing legal framework governing attempted suicide in Nigeria, shifting the approach towards support for affected persons. The bill is expected to be considered by the House in line with its legislative procedures. nigeria.description: Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, has urged the Federal Government to mount diplomatic pressure on the British Government to pay £420 million in damages awarded by a Federal High Court to the families of 21 coal miners killed in the 1949 Iva Valley massacre in Enugu State. Falana also called on the Federal Government to withdraw its appeal against the judgment, arguing that the British Government had not challenged the historic decision. He made the call in a statement marking the 75th anniversary of the massacre, in which 21 Nigerian coal miners were shot dead by colonial authorities during a protest against harsh working conditions, racial discrimination in wages and unpaid back wages. The judgment was delivered by Justice Anthony Onovo of the Federal High Court in the suit, Mazi Greg Onoh v. Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs & Ors (Suit No. E/909/2024). Justice Onovo held the British colonial administration liable for the killings, describing the massacre as an unlawful and extrajudicial violation of the right to life. The court ordered the British Government to pay £20 million to the families of each of the 21 deceased miners, amounting to £420 million in compensation. The judge found that the miners were defenceless and were merely demanding improved working conditions when they were shot, stressing that they were not engaged in any violent action against the authorities. The court also awarded post-judgment interest of 10 per cent per annum on the compensation until full payment, while claims for pre-judgment interest and exemplary damages were waived. In addition, Justice Onovo ordered the British Government to issue unreserved written apologies to the victims’ families through their counsel. The apologies are to be published in Nigeria’s Daily Sun, Daily Independent and The Punch, as well as three major national newspapers in the United Kingdom. The court directed that evidence of the publications be filed within 60 days, while the monetary awards must be satisfied within 90 days of the judgment. Justice Onovo further held that the Federal Government and the Attorney-General of the Federation had a constitutional responsibility under Sections 19(d) and 150(1) to pursue redress for the victims. He faulted the prolonged failure of the Nigerian authorities to seek justice for the deceased miners, describing the inaction as a dereliction of their constitutional responsibility. The judge consequently directed the Federal Government to initiate and pursue diplomatic engagement with the British authorities within 60 days to secure justice, effective remedies and reparations. Falana urged the Federal Government to concentrate on enforcing the judgment rather than pursuing an appeal, insisting that the families of the slain miners deserved justice and compensation for the killings. nigeria.title: US applauds Nigerian troops for rescuing 125 kidnap victims
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The United States has commended Nigerian troops for rescuing 125 kidnap victims during military operations across the country between November 6 and 12. The US Bureau of African Affairs gave the commendation in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday, also praising the troops for dismantling terrorist camps, recovering weapons and clearing explosive devices. “The United States commends Nigerian military operations this month that have rescued 125 kidnapping victims, along with the dismantling of Islamic terrorist camps, the recovery of weapons, and clearance of explosive devices,” the statement read. The bureau said Washington supported the Federal Government’s efforts to prevent kidnappings and ensure those responsible were brought to justice. “We support all efforts by the Nigerian government to prevent kidnappings and hold the perpetrators of this violence fully accountable,” it added. The Defence Headquarters had earlier disclosed that troops rescued the 125 victims during operations conducted between November 6 and 12. It said the troops also killed eight terrorists and arrested 10 suspected collaborators and logistics suppliers during the operations. The military said the largest rescue operation took place in Borno State, where troops freed 119 travellers abducted on November 6 along the Dutsen Kura-Bulazarma-Kamuya Road in Buratai, Biu Local Government Area. According to the military, the attackers abandoned the captives while fleeing from pursuing troops. Those rescued comprised 69 men, 35 women and 15 children. Troops also rescued five kidnapped persons in separate operations in Zamfara State. The military further disclosed that 12 terrorist fighters and members of their families surrendered during the operations. nigeria.title: UK warns visa applicants against four fraud red flags
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom Visas and Immigration (UKVI) agency has warned foreign nationals applying for British visas to watch out for four warning signs that could indicate fraud. The agency issued the advisory in a post on its X handle on Wednesday, urging applicants to protect themselves against visa scams and fraudulent agents. “4 RED FLAGS to watch out for when applying for a UK visa. Protect yourself from visa fraud by learning these crucial warning signs in our infographic,” UKVI said. The warning signs include individuals who guarantee applicants UK visas or jobs, offer appointments or visa services that cannot be verified through official channels, make unsolicited contact to demand money or personal information, and pressure applicants to act immediately or keep transactions secret. According to the agency, scammers operate through phone calls, websites, emails and social media platforms, while some also approach unsuspecting applicants outside visa application centres. It said fraudsters often impersonate Home Office officials or representatives of visa application centres, offering to secure jobs, arrange appointments or process visa applications. Some also claim that there is a problem with an applicant’s visa and demand urgent payment to prevent its cancellation or possible deportation. UKVI warned that fraudsters could use official-sounding language and forged documents, including seemingly genuine job offer letters, to convince applicants to part with their money. The agency also cautioned against agents who promise to fast-track visa applications in exchange for payments into personal bank accounts. “Visa officers will never ask you for money in person, by email or phone,” the guidance stated. It added that applicants seeking UK visas or permission to travel would never be asked to pay visa fees through email, at a visa application centre or into a personal bank account. The agency advised applicants to book appointments through the official UK government website or its authorised commercial partner. It further warned that submitting forged documents could result in visa refusal and a 10-year ban on future UK visa applications. UKVI urged applicants who suspect fraud not to disclose personal information, surrender their passports or send money, gift cards or vouchers to suspected scammers. It advised victims and individuals who suspect fraud in the UK to report the incidents to Report Fraud, while those outside the country should contact their local authorities. Visa fraud remains a concern for international travellers, with applicants sometimes losing money to fraudulent agents and unauthorised service providers. nigeria.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries for House speaker
nigeria.description: US Democrats on Wednesday elected Hakeem Jeffries as their leader and nominee for Speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on course to become the first Black politician to occupy the powerful position. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 votes cast against his nomination, according to US media reports. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressive lawmakers exposed divisions within the Democratic Party over how to exercise its newfound power following a sweeping midterm election victory. His nomination positions him to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as the party prepares to reverse Republican policies and launch investigations into the administration. However, Jeffries must still secure a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3. With Democrats holding a large majority, his election is widely expected to be a formality. Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s leadership election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics. Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination by acclamation, a process that would have allowed the party to endorse him without a formal ballot. He argued that every Democrat should have the opportunity to assess his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018. Although the overall voting figures were made public, individual ballots remained secret. Ahead of the election, Jeffries met with progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare. Proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand healthcare coverage were among the issues considered. The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to his party’s governing agenda following the Republican defeat, amid voter dissatisfaction over the Iran war and rising fuel costs. “Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters on Tuesday. “We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.” Brooklyn roots Raised in the working-class Crown Heights neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York State Legislature in 2007. He was elected to Congress in 2012. Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and frequent references to hip-hop artists, he made history in 2022 when Democrats elected him to succeed Nancy Pelosi as their House leader, making him the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress. nigeria.title: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The military has defended its engagement with armed bandits in Kwara State, dismissing allegations of fraternisation with terrorists. They added that the interaction led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The Joint Task Force, Operation Savannah Shield, said the engagement, captured in a video circulating on social media, was part of a security initiative to recover illegal weapons and secure the freedom of abducted persons. In a statement, the task force said the interaction involving military personnel, Department of State Services (DSS) operatives and the armed bandits should not be misconstrued as a compromise of the Armed Forces’ responsibilities. The statement, signed by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 9 Division/Operation Savannah Shield, Lieutenant Colonel Ibrahim Shittu, said the armed elements had indicated their willingness to surrender their weapons and release their captives. Shittu said the development followed sustained military operations that had put the bandits under intense pressure, leaving them with the options of surrendering or being neutralised. He said the engagement resulted in the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The task force described the outcome as evidence of the effectiveness of its non-kinetic approach, which complements ongoing military offensives against terrorism and banditry. It explained that its operational strategy combined military action, intelligence-driven engagements and other non-kinetic measures to address security challenges. The task force added that individuals willing to surrender would undergo appropriate security screening and other applicable legal procedures. Shittu also said surrendered combatants must not be harmed at the point of surrender, in line with the Law of Armed Conflict, international best practices and established rules of engagement. He stressed that accepting the surrender of armed elements was a recognised and legitimate military outcome, not an indication of unprofessional conduct or compromise. The task force reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to defending Nigeria’s territorial integrity and protecting lives and property. It urged members of the public to disregard what it described as misleading interpretations of the video and avoid spreading unverified information capable of undermining ongoing security operations. Operation Savannah Shield assured Nigerians that it would continue to provide updates on its activities through its official communication channels. nigeria.title: Army commissions 20 transit flats, officers’ mess in Bauchi
nigeria.description: By Henry Obetta The Nigerian Army has commissioned 20 transit flats and a modern officers’ mess at Obienu Barracks, Bauchi State, as part of efforts to improve personnel welfare, boost troops’ morale and enhance operational effectiveness. The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, who commissioned the facilities on Wednesday, said the Army’s modernisation drive went beyond the acquisition of military equipment to include improved accommodation, infrastructure and welfare for personnel and their families. According to a statement by the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, Shaibu described decent accommodation and a conducive living environment as critical to troops’ morale, family stability and operational readiness. He explained that the 20 transit flats were designed to address accommodation challenges faced by personnel posted to the barracks for assignments, military courses and other temporary engagements. The COAS said the newly constructed officers’ mess, named the Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu Officers’ Mess, featured modern accommodation, a Hall of Fame and recreational facilities to promote professional interaction, esprit de corps and institutional pride among officers. He commended the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps and other stakeholders for the successful completion of the projects, describing them as evidence of the Army’s commitment to personnel welfare and prudent management of resources. Shaibu urged personnel to ensure proper maintenance of the facilities to guarantee their sustainability and continued usefulness. Reaffirming his commitment to the welfare of troops and their families, the Army chief said investments in accommodation, healthcare, education and other welfare programmes would continue alongside the force’s expansion and modernisation efforts. He stressed that a well-motivated, professionally trained and adequately supported force was essential to sustaining operational successes against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other security threats facing the country. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds Binance says it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers. Reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to. “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss said. What is frozen Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report . That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it says was affected. Most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts. The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice says government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva said the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action. How the hack unfolded Binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the company said. From there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance. The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has said the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster. That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. The stolen BTC is not covered by those freezes and can be stopped only if it reaches an exchange or service that blocks it. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam Coinbase (COIN) said its AI scam-prevention agent stopped about $4.7 million in customer funds from reaching scammers who used a deepfake of Elon Musk to pitch a fake Tesla crypto giveaway, blocking roughly 91% of the money customers tried to send. The exchange described the incident in a Tuesday blog post, part of a weekly series on consumer protection. It said the system worked “with no humans in the loop.” Those two figures imply customers tried to send about $5.2 million, and that roughly $460,000 still left their accounts. Coinbase did not say how much reached the scammers. A livestream that wasn’t real The scam ran during Tesla’s “flying car” demo. Scammers set up a YouTube livestream that looked like the real broadcast, with a deepfake Musk, on-screen wallet addresses and a QR code. The stream promised to double any crypto sent to it, and more than half a million people watched, Coinbase said. Over about two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers tried to send millions of dollars to the addresses on screen. Many were long-time users. Coinbase did not say when the fake stream ran or which coins customers tried to send. The company stressed that its platform was not breached. “Nobody was hacked,” Coinbase wrote. “No Coinbase account was broken into, no password stolen, no credential phished.” That is what makes giveaway fraud hard to stop, since most defenses look for activity the account holder did not authorize, and here the customers logged in and pressed confirm themselves. “Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent,” the post said. How the agent works Coinbase said its defense has three parts. Machine learning models first score outgoing sends in real time, watching for giveaway patterns, brand impersonation and newly created wallet addresses. The goal, the company wrote, is “to catch the danger, not the customer.” When a send is flagged, a scam-specific agent takes over, looking up context, naming the scam pattern, explaining how giveaway schemes work and asking questions meant to make the story fall apart. Each reply is scored for confidence before the customer sees it, so the system knows when a situation needs more friction. The agent had never been trained on this kind of con, Coinbase said. Deepfake giveaways tied to a live product launch were not in its training data. “It recognized the shape of the scheme anyway,” the company wrote, pointing to the promise to multiply funds, the deadline of a live event and a transfer that could not be reversed. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says South Korea’s Financial Services Commission plans to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report . The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release. The FSC itself has not publicly announced a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025. A roadmap that stalled That plan opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit. Exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived. The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate. What the Basic Act adds The Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week. Lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Min Byung-duk of the Democratic Party said at a recent forum that he intends to “wrap it up by Jan. 9.” The 5% question The report did not describe what the corporate guidelines will contain. entertainment.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings. After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it " shameful " and a " national embarrassment ." News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases , more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases . There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week. But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. technology.title: California tells Waymo to take the next exit after freeway mishaps
technology.description: Waymo has suspended driverless freeway rides across the US after California regulators intervened over robotaxis entering construction zones and trying to bypass highway patrol vehicles. California's DMV banned Waymo from offering driverless trips on its freeways on Wednesday, November 11. The same day, Waymo pulled the handbrake on its freeway services countrywide. The move affects all areas in which Waymo operates on freeways, including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, Phoenix, and Austin. The Alphabet-owned company has not indicated how long the suspension will last. Waymo says freeway testing will continue with trained specialists behind the wheel. Jonathan Groveman, spokesperson for the California DMV, told the Associated Press that the organization imposed the ban following two incidents involving Waymo's robotaxis that posed an "imminent hazard to public safety." On November 5, three of the company's driverless cars entered an active construction zone on US 101 near Burlingame, south of San Francisco. The second incident occurred the following day, and in footage shared widely online , a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to drive around highway patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break – a maneuver used to slow or stop traffic. "The Department determined that Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present," Groveman said in the statement. Groveman said the DMV had already imposed restrictions and required corrective action following similar incidents on May 18. Waymo subsequently recalled nearly 4,000 cars after some were caught ignoring road closure signs and cones designating construction zones in Phoenix and San Francisco. A separate recall covered software affecting nearly 3,800 robotaxis over problems including slowing on high-speed roadways and driving into floodwater . A Waymo spokesperson said that despite California's temporary ban, its robotaxis continue to operate on city streets across the US. "Safety is at the foundation of everything we do," they said. "Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on US 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. "We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations." Other nuisances and hazards caused by errant Waymos include clogging traffic in thick fog , driving into telephone poles , and killing cats and dogs . ®

technology.title: Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
technology.description: Microsoft’s official agent framework package hosted on PyPI has been hijacked and now installs info-stealing malware, multiple security research firms have discovered. CEO Satya Nadella may be on stage trying to wow investors and customers at his company’s annual Ignite conference , but somewhere in the bowels of a building in Redmond his open source team is likely panicking at what appears to be unauthorized access to an administrator account on Microsoft’s Github organization. The problem package is Microsoft’s agent-framework, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, researchers reported late yesterday and this morning . According to OX Security, version 1.26.1 was reverted to a safe version, but the attacker later uploaded 1.26.2 through Microsoft’s official PyPI publisher account, suggesting that, at least at the time of their report, the credentials hadn’t been locked down. Safe to say, but if you find either version in your environment assume you have some account security work to do. Microsoft agent-framework for Python boasts nearly 200,000 downloads a month and is used to build and deploy AI agents. As of those latest releases, it’s also being used to exfiltrate environment variables, credential files, and other secrets for Azure, Git, Docker, Hugging Face, and other sensitive developer services. To make matters worse, the package never needs to be imported to do its dirty work – all it takes is a Python interpreter with the package installed to start up – the infected package still pulls the genuine 1.26.0 version of Microsoft’s agent-framework in order to keep itself running and looking legitimate, while in the background it gathers up credentials, encrypts them as a base64-encoded chunk of JSON, and sends them off to a webhook.site address hard coded into the malware. It appears from researcher accounts that this is made to act fast, as the malware isn’t persistent and only runs as long as the malicious version of the agent-framework remains in a site-packages directory. What it does do, however, is not just look for credentials in the environment: It actually starts calling for new ones and collecting them, too. In particular, the malware requests fresh identity tokens from GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Azure itself, which are exfiltrated to the same webhook site. “That combination of passive theft and active token requests makes it especially dangerous in cloud build environments, because even short-lived tokens are useful when they're exfiltrated right away,” said researchers at OpenSourceMalware. The agent-framework GitHub repo is offline as of writing. It’s been pointed out online that Microsoft’s repo for ONNX Runtime , an AI accelerator, is also offline. technology.title: MongoDB snaps up Firebolt to bring transactions and analytics under one roof
technology.description: MongoDB has acquired analytical database specialist Firebolt in another attempt to bring transactional and analytical workloads onto one platform. The document database vendor carved out its patch of the database market with flexible, JSON-like documents rather than rigid, predefined table structures. Developers put it to work in web, mobile, ecommerce, and content management applications. It has since branched out to offer a data platform it says is ready for the age of AI and AI agents working across transactional environments, promising scale, speed and reliability. Firebolt was founded in Israel in 2019. It built a cloud-native data warehouse based on the notion of automatically and transparently merging and compacting files as they are ingested. Speaking to The Register in 2020 , then CTO Eldad Farkash claimed this slashes the amount of data users need to load into the system, accelerating query performance and improving concurrency. Firebolt raised $100 million in Series C funding in 2022 at a reported valuation of $1.4 billion. MongoDB has not disclosed the acquisition price. But what will it get, and what does that mean for MongoDB users? In a blog post , the company said: "By integrating Firebolt into MongoDB's Intelligent Data Platform, we're bringing a high-performance analytics engine to where your operational data already lives. Firebolt's engine will run right alongside your database, and we'll keep it in sync automatically, so there's no pipeline to build or manage. You'll get one platform for operational and real-time analytical workloads, so teams can ship faster, with fewer systems to operate and secure." The integration isn't available yet. MongoDB says customers will gain access in the coming months, while existing Firebolt customers will retain their current service and support. MongoDB's pitch is that AI agents will need fresh operational data and fast analytical answers, without customers having to stitch separate platforms together. MongoDB is hardly the first vendor to chase that combination. Bringing online transaction processing (OLTP) and online analytical processing (OLAP) together promises less infrastructure to manage and fewer data pipelines to maintain. Delivering both without compromises is the harder part. Earlier this year, Databricks claimed to have cracked the problem , promising "one data, zero compromises, zero copies." It works with Reyden – a new compute engine – and Lakebase, its serverless PostgreSQL on open object storage. Rivals pointed out there were briefly two copies of the data in the system at some level. SingleStore also tackles the problem with an in-memory row store and an on-disk column store with tiered storage, "meaning transactions hit memory first, and then they roll off to disk storage," allowing analytics and transactions on a single system. science.description: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The Hall thruster is part of an Solar Electric Propulsion (SEP) system that uses 10 times less propellant than equivalent chemical rockets. Image Credit: NASA/Michelle M. Murphy (Wyle Information Systems, LLC) NASA launched a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration. Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical for space operations and exploration. NASA’s Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge is offering $500,000, split between two winning U.S. companies, to accelerate the maturation of mid-power systems that could be foundational to supporting future NASA and commercial missions. Interested parties can learn more at an AMPERE Virtual Industry Day hosted by NASA on Thursday, Nov. 19. “This challenge approach seeks to remove key barriers and facilitate commercialization by providing access to NASA subject matter expertise, state-of-the-art technologies, and world-class facilities at no cost to challenge winners,” said Dr. Jason Frieman, AMPERE project co-owner at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland. “We hope participants will see this as an opportunity to demonstrate their capabilities to NASA and other government and commercial stakeholders.” The competition is the first of NASA’s Tech Maturation Prize series, which seeks to accelerate development of breakthrough technologies in support of NASA missions while strengthening the U.S. space economy. The competition includes three phases. In Phase 1, each participating team will submit a concept design, manufacturing plan, and cost and performance projections. NASA may select two winners to advance to Phase 2, where teams will develop prototypes and collaborate with NASA personnel. Through no-cost licensing, these teams can gain early access to NASA-developed Hall effect thruster technologies that use krypton as a propellant. In Phase 3, prototypes will be tested at NASA Glenn at no cost to the participating teams. In total, two winning teams may be selected to receive up to $250,000 each. The AMPERE Challenge is open for registration until Jan. 27, 2027, at 5 p.m. EST. The challenge supports the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket project, managed by NASA Glenn and NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The project is funded by the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate . science.title: New Scientist is 70 years old – join us in celebrating
science.description: Julianna Funk/Alamy Break open the bubbly, light the candles and get ready to party – New Scientist is 70 years old! Times have certainly changed since we published our first issue in 1956. Back then, some scientists had proposed that our carbon dioxide emissions were warming the planet, but the idea was controversial. Biologists were only beginning to unpick how DNA, whose structure had just been elucidated by Francis Crick, James Watson, Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, encoded the instructions for building organisms. The founders of this magazine couldn’t have envisaged the many ways that the web and smartphones would change daily life. We are even old enough that what once seemed futuristic is now pleasantly quaint. Launching our first website, Planet Science , in 1995, we declared that, “As the technologies mature, quite soon and at a terminal near you, it may be possible to hear interviews with well-known scientists”. Our digital offering has expanded greatly since then, with these sorts of interviews now available across our podcast and video channels. That said, we also speculated that it might be possible to “manipulate three-dimensional models of molecules” on a future version of our website, which we still haven’t quite managed to deliver. To mark our anniversary, we have put together a timeline of the biggest breakthroughs of the past 70 years . I enjoyed diving into our archives in search of how we reported era-defining moments. Our assessments haven’t always been on the money: after Yuri Gagarin’s space flight in 1961, for example, our correspondent declared “it is almost physically impossible for [the US] to beat the Russians to the moon”. Advertisement The secret to New Scientist ‘s longevity is a devoted following of readers A clear demonstration, if one were needed, that most predictions turn out to be wrong. But looking ahead is in New Scientist ‘s DNA, so, bravely – or foolishly – we press on. The main feature in this special issue is a trip to the year 2096, seven decades from now, for an imagined article for our 140th anniversary . To make our predictions as informed as possible, Jacob Aron consulted a panoply of scientists for their views and wove it all together to create one plausible path for the future . Sometimes, it turns out that fiction writers can see the future more accurately than scientists. Emily H. Wilson has trawled through 70 years of sci-fi in search of the most prescient predictions . Robert A. Heinlein, Ursula K. Le Guin, Octavia E. Butler and Cixin Liu are among those who have shown remarkable foresight. Of course, the secret to New Scientist’s longevity is a devoted following who have been with us since the days of Daedalus, Enigma and Grimbledon Down. science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Past times That creaking sound you just heard was Feedback’s ageing joints as we painfully sat down to type out this commemorative column. We have been here for a considerable number of decades, to the point that our recollection of our earliest missives has become faded and confused. Indeed, Feedback’s history is long and storied, to the point that it would defy the efforts of even the most conscientious biographer. We have been through many incarnations, most of whom went on to do far more felicitous things with their lives. It is a little-discussed fact, one not even known to reality, that a previous Feedback helped David Foster Wallace out by composing Infinite Jest over the course of a bank holiday weekend. We’re told that former Feedbacks also secretly performed the guitar solos on Stairway to Heaven and Killing in the Name . Advertisement For these reasons, most incarnations of Feedback were and are anonymous. Indeed, the identity of the current Feedback is known only to the king, the prime minister and the head of MI5. This anonymity has its drawbacks: our collective memory only stretches back so far. Thankfully, our editor took it upon themselves to venture into the New Scientist archive, in search of the first Feedbacks. It is difficult to fully convey what the archive is like, but if you imagine the warehouse at the end of Raiders of the Lost Ark and then insert a leaking roof and a surfeit of rats, your mental image will not be too badly astray. Escaping with only a minor amputation and an urgent need to be vaccinated, the editor delivered to us pages from the very first New Scientist . Fetal Feedback There is no Feedback, but there is a column called “It Seems to Me”, written by an anonymous person known only as “Geminus”. This was the proto-Feedback, and it might best be described as a relic of a bygone age. science.title: Are these the most spectacular and intriguing beetles in the world?
science.description: The glorious flower chafer Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum What animal is older than the dinosaurs and accounts for nearly a quarter of species on Earth? It is the magnificent beetle, an insect whose wings rest underneath a hard, protective case that often displays beautiful colours and intricate ornaments. “Wherever you stand on the land surface of the Earth save only for Antarctica, you are never more than a few metres from a beetle,” writes Maxwell Barclay in Interesting Beetles , which showcases some of their stunning variety. The main image shows the glorious flower chafer ( Howdenypa gloriosa ), a stunning opalescent green and blue. Its sleek flight from flower to flower, which takes place with the wing cases closed, unlike the clumsier flights of beetles with open wing cases, has attracted attention from aerospace engineers. They have fitted some flower chafers with tiny wireless transmitters to better understand how they manoeuvre while flying. Below is the Colorado potato beetle ( Leptinotarsa decemlineata ), which has a destructive relationship with humans. After the potato was introduced to North America, this striped beetle started to prefer spuds to native foods and quickly became a worldwide pest. Advertisement The Colorado potato beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Below, the carbuncle frog-legged beetle ( Sagra carbunculus ) shows off the buff hind legs that earned it its amphibian-inspired name and serve it well in battle – or when competing for an iridescent mate. The carbuncle frog-legged beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum The specimens in these images are taken from the archives of the Natural History Museum in London, where Barclay is senior curator in charge of beetles. It was difficult, he writes in his book, to choose which to include, “because each of the 400,000 beetle species has an interesting story to tell”. The violin beetle ( Mormolyce phyllodes ) shown below makes up for being an inelegant flyer by having a unique body shape that allows it to blend in with fallen leaves and winged seeds of trees in the steamy tropical rainforests where it resides. The violin beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Finally, the desert fog-basking beetle ( Onymacris bicolor ) shown below is another master of adaptation that can survive in places as arid and harsh as the Namib desert in southern Africa. Elegant in its black-and-white garb, this insect climbs to the top of a dune when conditions are right, points its head down and waits for dew to condense on special structures on its wings and then run into its mouth, keeping it alive. The desert fog-basking beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Barclay writes that beetles can not only survive in all these habitats, from potato fields to tropical forests and deserts, but that they are an integral part of each of them. science.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
science.description: null United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28 , and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.) ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update. Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit. In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance. Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure. Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

science.title: What Is the Moon Base?
science.description: 7 Min Read What Is the Moon Base? This article is for students. NASA is returning astronauts to the Moon – and this time they will spend more time on the lunar surface. The Moon Base is humanity’s first lunar outpost . It will be a place where astronauts live, work, and explore. Artist’s concept depicting astronauts, habitats, rovers, power systems, and cargo operations supporting sustained human activities at the Moon Base near the lunar South Pole. NASA ______________________________________________________________________ Words to Know outpost: a station or base located in a remote, distant place infrastructure: the basic framework and systems that make up a larger building or organization terrain: the physical features, shape, and layout of the surface of a piece of land, including its slope and elevation regolith : the layer of loose, fragmented rock and mineral dust covering most of the lunar surface ______________________________________________________________________ Where Will the Moon Base Be Built? The Moon Base will be built in the lunar South Pole region. This area was selected for its unique lighting conditions and potential for scientific discovery. Near the lunar South Pole, the Sun stays low on the horizon. Some areas can receive extended periods of sunlight. Other areas stay in shadows for long periods of time. In some craters, sunlight may never reach the surface at all. Areas that receive extended sunlight could be good for generating solar power. Longer sunlight hours are also good for navigating and exploring. Areas that remain in shadows are some of the coldest areas on the Moon. In these locations, scientists hope to find deposits of frozen water ice. When Will the Moon Base Be Constructed? The Moon Base will be constructed in three phases. Each phase will build on what is learned along the way. Phase One is taking place right now. Over the next few years, NASA and its partners will send robotic missions to explore the lunar South Pole region. They will test new technologies and practice landing on the Moon. This phase will include multiple different landers and lunar terrain vehicles. These missions will conduct science experiments and look for the best locations for building the Moon Base. Phase Two is planned for 2029-2032. During this period, NASA will begin setting up long-term infrastructure . This includes things like power systems, cargo transportation, and communications hardware. These components will be set up across multiple locations. This will allow for future expansion of the Moon Base. During Phase Three, NASA will begin assembling a permanent lunar outpost. This is where astronauts will be able to live and work for extended periods. Habitats, power and communication systems, and transportation will all come together to grow Moon Base. science.title: 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket?
science.description: null The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket. NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet . But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the " Mars Czar ") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com. "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'" Shotgun marriage? Hubbard is a retired adjunct professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University. He is a major voice in shaping Red Planet exploration goals, drawing upon his expertise as NASA's former foremost Mars authority. His understanding is that the basic concept had been developed as a follow on to Ingenuity, an attempt to move beyond a technology demo and into a science platform. Hubbard said that combining these two observations, the outcome presents "an unusual set of management issues." Since the SkyFall mission concept first appeared, he said, the usual sequence for a science mission is reversed. "The science community is having to scramble to back into a set of requirements and objectives that match the SkyFall capabilities. Fortunately the community is very creative," said Hubbard, "and the basic Planetary Decadal objectives are very broad." Decadal surveys reflect a broad consensus within the scientific community and provide detailed insights into the strategic priorities and mission directives set for the next decade across key scientific domains, including planetary exploration. Lemonade squeeze However, Hubbard said he has heard griping about the "fait accompli" process, "but the planetary community will make lemonade." It should be noted however, Hubbard continued, that this process is not how you would design a strategic set of missions as precursors for human exploration. "SR-1 Freedom is a technology demo that may or may not be ready for the Mars launch window in 2028. It is clear that the Mars Program has a standard launch concept in their back pocket," said Hubbard. science.title: Homo erectus survived on mainland Asia 215,000 years longer than we thought
science.description: Reconstruction of a specimen of Homo erectus S. ENTRESSANGLE/E. DAYNES/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY Preserved teeth from two caves in southern China indicate Homo erectus lived on mainland Asia as recently as 184,000 years ago. That is recent enough for the species to have met later groups like the Denisovans. It seems these Chinese H. erectus were living in a tropical rainforest – an environment where the species has not previously been found. “We’ve got this late surviving population, and we’ve got this rich story of how they were living,” says geochronologist Kira Westaway at Macquarie University in Sydney. Advertisement H. erectus was one of the first species in our genus, Homo . It was also the first species of hominin we know for sure migrated beyond Africa. The earliest H. erectus fossils are from Africa 2 million years ago, but by 1.8 million years ago they were living in what is now Georgia on the border between Europe and Asia. Eventually the species spread further east into what is now China. They even made it to the island of Java. Read more The 85-million-year timeline of human evolution The most recent fossils identified as H. erectus are from Java and are between 117,000 and 108,000 years old . However, it’s been thought the species vanished much earlier from mainland Asia. Until the discoveries from China announced today, the most recent securely dated H. erectus were from around 400,000 years ago. Around this time, other hominin groups emerged, like the Denisovans who lived in East Asia. “The assumption would have been that erectus is basically no longer there, because they have evolved into a Denisovan population,” says molecular palaeontologist Frido Welker at the University of Copenhagen in Denmark. Welker, Westaway and their colleagues investigated two caves in southern China. Baxian and Naxian are both limestone caves, about 15 kilometres apart. They were initially excavated by Chinese teams led by Yingqi Zhang at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing and Wei Wang at Shandong University. science.title: Quantum trick lets you share your location super securely
science.description: NIST’s campus in Boulder, Colorado NIST Financial institutions and critical infrastructure could be made far more secure in the near-future using quantum particles. For years, researchers have predicted that quantum particles could enable someone to share their location, and to verify someone else’s, in a way that is exceedingly difficult to hack. This would allow one branch of a bank to confirm that a request for funds or client information is coming from another branch and not from a hacker. Likewise, hackers could be stopped from trying to remotely control a power grid, a nuclear plant – or even commercial freezers, which have recently been hacked across Europe . Gautam Kavuri at the University of Colorado Boulder and his colleagues have now shown that quantum devices really can provide such location verification, offering a level of security impenetrable to most hackers. Advertisement Read more Inside the company selling quantum entanglement “From a security perspective, it’s sort of the gold-plated Rolls Royce of protocols. It’s got the best security you can have in principle, while making the least assumptions,” says team member Krister Shalm at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Colorado. “And you can actually do it.” In the researchers’ experiment, two verifier devices had to confirm the location of a third device called the prover. Each device was in a different location: the verifiers were 195 metres apart in different labs and the prover was in a third location between them. Kavuri says it was important for these devices to be in different rooms on the NIST campus, rather than all in the same lab, because this is closer to a practical scenario in the real world. The devices were connected with electrical cables and optical fibres and could exchange quantum particles of light that had been connected into pairs through the inextricable link of quantum entanglement . To begin the new quantum position verification (QPV) protocol, a verifier would send one photon from an entangled pair to the prover and, simultaneously, each verifier would also send a random number that instructed the prover on which particle property to measure. Next, the prover sent the outcome of that measurement to both verifiers. They used the time it took to receive this information to calculate the prover’s position. First, quantum information, such as that carried by particles of light, can never be copied or cloned surreptitiously . Additionally, the researchers leveraged a procedure called a Bell test , which is specific to entangled particles, and would be failed if a hacker tampered with them. The net effect was that any conventional strategy for faking the position would set off one of these quantum safeguards. science.title: Supernova explodes before astronomers' eyes | Space photo of the day for Nov. 18, 2026
science.description: null Before-and-after photos showing the appearance of a new supernova designated SN 2026ahvu. (Image credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Acknowledgment: PIs: G. Narayan & T. Murphey (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign) Image processing: M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)) A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth. What is it? Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf . During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion. Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter. This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place. Why is it incredible? Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres. ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system. But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova. Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.
